title: August: Changing Daily Habits
coreMove: Change the habit by naming the trigger before obeying the urge; alcohol, take-out coffee, and shopping can all become comfort loops when discomfort goes unhandled.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers tracing the first emotional association behind a habit
exampleSpecs.stakes: An early confusing event can become a later coping script.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how the age 12 drink with the biological father links alcohol to confusion and adulthood.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse a crisis decision with finished change
exampleSpecs.stakes: A frightening event can start change while daily trigger work still remains.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the age 27 blackout as evidence that drinking has become dangerous.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers dismissing small purchases as harmless
exampleSpecs.stakes: A minor daily habit can stay invisible until repetition exposes its cost and trigger.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Make take-out coffee visible as a lower-stakes habit loop during the shopping ban.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose purchase cravings follow identity threat
exampleSpecs.stakes: Buying can promise a repaired self-image while leaving the original sting untouched.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Trace a shopping urge back to the feeling that activated it.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who use routine purchases to create transitions
exampleSpecs.stakes: A harmless purchase can hide the need for rest, reward, or transition.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the August take-out coffee habit to practice pausing before a purchase.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers replacing one comfort with another
exampleSpecs.stakes: A cleaner response should meet the feeling rather than merely change the object.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a response chosen after the trigger has already been named.
